name: api-design
title: API design
summary: Design, document and evolve HTTP APIs and webhooks: style choice, request and response contracts, errors, pagination, idempotency, rate limits, versioning and a public developer platform.
useWhen: Design the API for this feature, or review my endpoint design
Should this be REST, GraphQL, tRPC or server functions?
Add pagination, filtering and a consistent error format
Make this POST safe to retry without creating duplicates
Add rate limiting and quotas per API key or tenant
Receive a third party's webhooks, or send webhooks to our customers
Change this API without breaking existing clients
Launch a public API with keys, docs and SDKs
Expose our product to AI agents through MCP

notFor.topic: User login, sessions and permission models behind the endpoints
Service boundaries, background jobs and realtime transports
HTTP caching headers, CDN rules and edge rate limiting
Contract tests and other API test automation
Claude API parameters, tool-use syntax and SDK usage

references.title: Choosing and shaping an API style
references.purpose: Read when starting an API or adding a new surface: REST, typed RPC, GraphQL, gRPC or server functions, and how to describe it.

leaves.topic: Choose REST, typed RPC, GraphQL or server functions for each consumer
Design resources, names and URL structure consistently
Agree the API contract before implementing either side
Describe REST APIs in OpenAPI and generate typed clients
Design a GraphQL schema with complexity limits, batching and persisted queries
Use gRPC or Connect between internal services where it pays

references.title: Validation, errors, pagination and payloads
references.purpose: Read when defining what an endpoint accepts and returns: input validation, error shape, lists, filtering and data formats.

leaves.topic: Validate every input at the boundary against a schema
Return consistent RFC 9457 problem-details errors
Paginate every list endpoint with opaque cursors and stable ordering
Represent dates, money, IDs and enums unambiguously in JSON
Design filtering, sorting and field selection without exposing the schema
Cap body size, header size and request duration
Support partial updates with clear semantics for null and absent fields
Model long-running operations as job resources clients can poll
Report partial failure clearly in batch endpoints

references.title: Idempotency, concurrency control and rate limits
references.purpose: Read when clients may retry writes, edit the same resource concurrently, or need to be limited and metered.

leaves.topic: Make write endpoints safe to retry with client-supplied idempotency keys
Rate-limit per tenant and key with clear 429 and Retry-After responses
Store the request fingerprint and response so replays return the original result
Choose a rate-limit algorithm and store: token bucket, sliding window, Redis
Meter API usage per key and expose quotas in response headers
Use ETags and If-Match for optimistic concurrency on updates
Tell clients which errors to retry, with backoff and jitter
Cap expensive operations with cost-based limits and concurrency ceilings

references.title: Webhooks, inbound and outbound
references.purpose: Read when receiving events from another service or delivering events to customers' endpoints.

leaves.topic: Verify webhook signatures and reject replays
Acknowledge webhooks fast and process them asynchronously
Process webhooks idempotently, out of order and after delays
Reconcile missed webhooks by polling the source API
Send signed webhooks with retries, backoff and delivery logs
Deliver outbound webhooks without letting customer URLs reach internal networks
Let customers manage endpoints, secret rotation and event subscriptions
Version webhook payloads and choose thin or fat events

references.title: Versioning and evolving an API
references.purpose: Read before changing an API that has consumers you do not control, or when planning a deprecation.

leaves.topic: Evolve an API with additive changes and tolerant readers
Recognize which changes break clients before shipping them
Version a public API and publish a deprecation policy
Detect breaking changes by diffing the OpenAPI document in CI
Sunset an endpoint using usage data, response headers and customer notice
Run two API versions side by side with one implementation

references.title: Public API and developer platform
references.purpose: Read when opening the product to outside developers or agents: keys, docs, SDKs, sandbox, OAuth apps and MCP.

leaves.topic: Decide whether and when to commit to a public API
Issue scoped, expiring, hash-stored API keys customers can rotate
Publish API reference from OpenAPI with runnable examples

Ship versioned SDKs generated from the schema
Provide a sandbox or test mode separate from live data
Offer OAuth so third-party apps can act for your users
